knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operations involving broadcasting may not consistently handle zero-sized dimensions, especially when broadcast shapes are ambiguous or incompatible.

risk_dimensions.shape: Zero-sized dimensions in tensors participating in broadcasting

failure_mechanism.description: Shape validation or broadcasting logic does not correctly account for zero-sized dimensions, causing exceptions during operator invocation.

input_exploration: Explore zero-sized dimensions in tensors that participate in broadcasting
Vary broadcast compatibility between operands with empty shapes
Generate mismatched broadcast shapes where at least one dimension is zero
constraint_awareness: Zero-sized tensors are valid inputs but may expose shape boundary edge cases
Broadcasting rules with empty dimensions require special handling in shape validation
oracle_strategy: Compare observed behavior against broadcasting semantics and expected validation behavior
Detect unexpected exceptions or inconsistent exception behavior for shape boundary inputs

transferability.reason: Broadcasting with zero-sized dimensions is a general shape boundary concern affecting many APIs that accept tensor operands and rely on broadcast semantics.

important_considerations: Consider zero-sized dimensions and empty tensors when generating shape boundary inputs
Explore broadcast-compatible and broadcast-incompatible shape combinations that include zero dimensions
Treat exception behavior as a first-class oracle signal
generation_strategy: Generate diverse tensor shape combinations with zero-sized dimensions and use broadcasting rules as a reference oracle to detect inconsistent shape validation or unexpected exceptions.
